title: Change slate forensics playbook
summary: Working PRD draft for a forensics-oriented change playbook that stitches audit logs, approval gates, and customer-managed networking evidence into a compact, queryable change-slate for Private deployments.
body:
Status: draft. Audience: product, eng (platform & infra), SRE, security, solutions eng. Purpose: define an operator-friendly playbook + minimal API/telemetry contract that produces a compact change-slate for customer-managed networking changes in Private deployments. The goal is to make post-incident investigations and periodic audits efficient while minimizing customer telemetry surface and storage cost.

Problem statement:
- Private deployments mean customers control networking; we cannot forcibly capture all packet-level telemetry. When a customer reports a VPC/networking incident (connectivity regression, route leak, DNS misconfig), investigations today pull scattered artifacts (control-plane config snapshots, customer-submitted logs, partial attestation tokens).
- Current approval gate artifacts are verbose and not standardized, making triage slow and error-prone.
- Audit retention and storage cost constraints push teams to sample or compress logs, but compressed artifacts lose forensic fidelity.

Desired outcomes:
1) A standardized, small "change-slate" artifact that bundles the minimal cryptographic evidence and pointers needed to reconstruct a network-change event end-to-end within 72 hours.
2) Integration with approval gates so every authorized change can emit a change-slate at commit time (can be optional for low-trust tiers but mandatory for SLA-backed customers).
3) Clear UX for operators to request/receive slates from customers and to attach slates to incident postmortems.
4) Telemetry and retention guidance that balances privacy and forensics cost.

Non-goals:
- We are not building full packet capture or any customer-side remote collection agent.
- Not addressing application-layer audit beyond correlation pointers (e.g., request IDs).

Proposed concept (high level):
- Change-slate: a small, signed bundle containing: change metadata (who, when, what), approval evidence (signed approval token or approval digest), compact control-plane snapshot diff (CID or gzipped delta), outbound pointers (S3/approved archive URLs or customer-provided URIs), optional minimal telemetry hash-set (KV of sampled event hashes) and an integrity manifest (signature + hash chain).
- Emission points: when an operator or customer performs an authorized VPC/network change via the Private control-plane, the control-plane will produce a change-slate and store it in the customer-scoped evidence ledger (configurable retention). For manual, out-of-band changes we provide an ingestion API and a guided upload UX for customers to attach their pre-signed slate.

Operator flow (happy path):
1) Operator initiates VPC change in private-console (or infra-as-code with control-plane API).
2) Approval gate runs policy -> approver signs through Redwood delegated-approval service.
3) On commit, control-plane captures a compact diff of the VPC config and runtime routing table snapshot (limited fields), hashes each artifact, generates a manifest, signs it with control-plane key, and emits the change-slate.
4) Slate stored in customer evidence bucket and indexed in the immutable evidence ledger (searchable by change id, time, approver).
5) If a rollback is triggered, rollback event references the change-id and links both slates (change + rollback).

Manual ingestion flow (customer-provided adjustments):
- Customer-run change (outside control-plane) -> customer calls evidence ingestion API with pre-signed bundle and attestation token from their side. Ingestion validates signatures and links to existing tenant ledger entry (or creates new one).

Minimal slate schema (human-readable outline):
- change_id: short unique (e.g., sl-20260212-03)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- initiator: email or service-id
- approvers: list of approver ids (short)
- approved_policy: policy-id or slug
- diff_summary: one-line description (e.g., "add route 10.0.0.0/16 -> gw-3")
- artifacts: list of artifact pointers (s3://, gs://, or customer-uri) + artifact_hash
- manifest_hash: sha256(manifest)
- signatures: control_plane_sig (base64), optionally customer_sig
- retention_hint: days (per-customer override)

Note: We'll store full artifact content only for hosted evidence buckets (for Dedicated customers on Redwood-managed storage). For customer-managed buckets we store pointers and a signed assertion over the pointer.

API sketches (examples):
- POST /v1/tenants/{t}/evidence/slates  (emit slate)
  payload: {change_id, manifest, artifacts[] (pointer + hash), signatures[] }
- GET /v1/tenants/{t}/evidence/slates/{change_id}  (retrieve)
- POST /v1/tenants/{t}/evidence/ingest  (customer upload, validate signatures)
- GET /v1/tenants/{t}/evidence/search?q=...  (index search over metadata fields)

Retention & cost model:
- Default retention: 90 days of stored artifacts for hosted evidence; metadata + pointers retained indefinitely (7+ years for enterprise by request).
- For customers using customer-managed buckets we store only metadata and integrity signatures; retention cost is then on the customer.
- Compactification modes: full (store raw artifact, compute quick snapshots), delta (store compressed diffs), pointer-only (store no artifact). Product config per customer tier.

UX and tooling requirements:
- Console view: change timeline with attached slate, artifact list, preview of diff_summary, signer list, and quick-download for artifacts available in hosted buckets.
- Operator runbook template for triage: step-by-step to gather slates, verify signatures, fetch artifacts, run local diff tool. Include a small tool (redwood-evidence-cli) to validate slates locally (checks signatures, downloads pointers if permitted, prints consolidated timeline).
- Templates for PMs and SREs to add change-slate id to incident tasks and postmortems.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Control-plane emits valid slates on every change initiated through control-plane for pilot customers (>=95% of changes emit without error).
- Evidence ingestion API accepts pre-signed slates and attaches them to tenant ledger (validation coverage: signature check, pointer format, manifest hash).
- Console surfaces slate metadata and allows download of hosted artifacts.
- redwood-evidence-cli can verify a slate and list artifacts.
- Documentation + runbook exist and one pilot customer has completed a full incident replay using slates.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement and test server-side slate generation in staging (Q1 pilot).
2) Soft-launch to 2 pilot tenants (security-sensitive customers) with hosted evidence buckets and 90-day retention.
3) Iterate on schema and CLI based on pilot feedback (Q2).
4) Add customer-managed bucket pointer contract and ingestion UX (Q3).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers concerned about storing artifacts in Redwood-managed buckets. Mitigation: pointer-only mode, strong encryption and per-customer keys, explicit consent during onboarding.
- Risk: Signature/attestation complexity for customer-provided slates. Mitigation: provide SDK helpers and minimal recommended attestation scheme (HMAC-based alternative for lower-trust customers).
- Risk: Evidence bucket becomes a compliance liability. Mitigation: retention policies, legal review, JIT export for customer audits, and strong access controls + audit logs.

Open questions (decisions needed):
- Should change-slates include a small sampled packet-level hash (privacy vs usefulness)?
- How many artifact classes must Redwood store for hosted evidence vs pointer-only scenarios?
- Signing key model: one global control-plane signing key per region or per-tenant delegated signing with KMS per tenant?
- SLA implications: make slate emission mandatory for SLA tier X? Which tier?

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Engineering (Liam): prototype manifest generation + signature (due 2026-01-15).
- Security (Sana): threat model and key management recommendation (due 2026-01-22).
- Solutions (Diego): run pilot with 2 customers and gather feedback template (start 2026-02-01).
- Product (Marta): consolidate pilot feedback and author v1 PRD for exec review (due 2026-03-10).

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Consider a lightweight evidence index format that can be exported as a single JSONL for auditors.
- Explore integrating small ML model that can cluster slates for recurring flaky-change patterns (future).
- Slack reference: #private-deploy-evidence.

Quick references:
- related PRD sketches: CONFLUENCE-1452 (approval evidence index)
- relevant tickets: JIRA-PRV-879 (ingest API), JIRA-PRV-904 (retention config), GH-ops#412 (cli proof-of-concept).

This doc is intentionally compact — expect iterations. Use the playbook to reduce time-to-diagnosis and give customers confidence about auditability without overcollecting telemetry.
